recap.text: A man is taken apart in a cellar to get a spell to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, an undead wife sealed in a tomb who screams like a bird. Changelings want her body to wear her shape and cure compression sickness, while a banished deity intends to occupy her to be resurrected. Quetzalcoatlus attacks Carl and Vadim Zbar with a shriek on a submarine bridge. Morris Sp connects a submerged panel, using an electric shock to kill her.

A boss knocks Carl out of the sky over the forest. Carl recognizes the shape of the creature, a vampire in the flesh the size of a flying giraffe with a beak as long as Carl is tall. It is the same type of mob as Quetzalcoatlus, the pterodactyl-like ghost of the previous floor.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.
beats.gist: The name Quetzalcoatlus surfaces from a man being taken apart in a cellar under Hump Town.

beats.headline: An empress in the walls
beats.text: Per Morris Sp of the subterranean quadrant: Anser was an emperor, and when he died, his court and his wife were sealed into the tomb with him, alive. The wife is Quetzalcoatlus. She is undead now, non-corporeal, able to pass through the tomb's walls, and she can be heard screaming, like a bird. Having failed the map quest, the tomb crawlers received a new one: find her and kill her. Nobody knows how to kill a ghost. Morris observes that she would probably be easier to kill with a body.
beats.gist: Quetzalcoatlus is an undead, non-corporeal empress who screams like a bird and passes through tomb walls.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.
beats.gist: Juice Box explains that changelings want Quetzalcoatlus for her shapes and a spell for compression sickness.

beats.headline: What the council is afraid of
beats.text: A letter from the council of Ghazi's college sets out the fear. What he summoned was not the god of lust but a banished lesser deity pretending to be him, and the scholars believe she only half crossed over. She will occupy the one creature nearby that stands equally between worlds: the ghost queen of the necropolis. If Quetzalcoatlus gains corporeal form, that deity is fully resurrected and the true gods are forced to react. The council's instruction is that Ghazi use the winding box to banish himself, and the entire necropolis, out of this world.
beats.gist: A letter states a banished lesser deity pretending to be the god of lust occupies the ghost queen.

beats.headline: Out of her tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is not confined to her tomb. She is on the flooded submarine's bridge, flickering between it and the chamber on the far side of the hull, and she does not like visitors. Her scream is an aural attack: one shriek through the bulkhead reddens Crawler Carl's vision and drops Vadim Zbar into the red. Then she shoots out of the side of the sub, strikes something enormous in the water below, and flies back toward the temple. The thing she struck comes for the sub.
beats.gist: Quetzalcoatlus flickers between a submarine bridge and a hull chamber and attacks with a scream.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.
beats.gist: A note from a flooded submarine body says Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock.

beats.headline: The panel in the tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is finished. Morris Sp went down the ladder to the submerged panel knowing what the next lightning strike would do to anyone still in the water, connected it, and the current did precisely what the cleric's journal said it would. The Subterranean Quadrant is liberated and the bubble pops. The notice hails Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi and Morris Sp, and then remembers that every crawler who started in that quadrant is dead. They were dealt one of the worst hands on the floor, and they finished the job anyway.
beats.gist: Morris Sp connects a submerged panel in a tomb, liberating the Subterranean Quadrant and popping the bubble.

beats.headline: Same kind of mob, in the flesh
beats.text: The boss that knocks Carl out of the sky over the forest is the same type of mob as Quetzalcoatlus, the pterodactyl-like ghost of the previous floor. Carl recognises the shape before he reads the name. This one is not a ghost, but it is still undead: a vampire in the flesh, like a pelican crossed with a vulture and the size of a flying giraffe, with a beak as long as Carl is tall.
beats.gist: A vampire boss the size of a flying giraffe knocks Carl out of the sky.
